calc-limits-01: Seedha $x=0$ daalo to $0/0$ aata hai. Numerator mein $1+3x$ to cancel ho jaata hai — dekho $e^{3x}$ ka kaunsa term bachta hai jo neeche ke $x^2$ se match kare.
Taylor: $e^{u}=1+u+\frac{u^2}{2}+\dots$, yahan $u=3x$. Limit sirf numerator ke $x^2$ wale term ka coefficient decide karega.
$\frac{u^2}{2}$ mein $u=3x$ daalo — square poore $3x$ ka hoga, sirf $x$ ka nahi. Phir $x^2$ se divide karo. Trap: L'Hôpital ek hi baar lagaya to abhi bhi $0/0$ hai.
calc-limits-02: $x\to0$ pe $\sin 5x$ aur $\tan 2x$ dono 0 hain — $0/0$ form. Arguments $5x$ aur $2x$ alag hain, isliye ratio ko seedha 1 mat maano.
Small $u$ ke liye $\frac{\sin u}{u}\to1$ aur $\frac{\tan u}{u}\to1$. Upar $u=5x$ aur neeche $u=2x$ lo.

Likho $\frac{\sin5x}{5x}\cdot\frac{2x}{\tan2x}\cdot(\text{ek factor})$ — pehle do factor 1 ki taraf jaate hain. Expression same rahe, iske liye bacha factor kya hona chahiye? Trap: ratio ulta (neeche wala upar) mat karna.
calc-limits-03: Base $1+\frac{2}{x}\to1$ aur exponent $3x\to\infty$ — ye $1^\infty$ form hai, iski value 1 nahi hoti.
$1^\infty$ rule: limit $=e^{L}$ jahan $L=\lim\,(f-1)\cdot g$. Yahan $f-1=\frac{2}{x}$ aur $g=3x$.
$L=\lim 3x\cdot\frac{2}{x}$ mein $x$ cancel karo, phir $e^{L}$ calculator se 2 decimal tak nikalo. Trap: constants ko multiply karna hai, add nahi ($e^{2+3}$ galat hai).
calc-limits-04: $x=0$ pe upar $1-\cos x$ aur neeche $x\sin x$ dono 0 — $0/0$. Dono ka leading power $x^2$ hai, unke coefficients compare karne hain.
Standard approximations: $1-\cos x\approx\frac{x^2}{2!}$ aur $\sin x\approx x$, isliye $x\sin x\approx x^2$.
Numerator ke coefficient mein $\frac{1}{2!}$ mat chhodo (log $x^2$ likh dete hain). L'Hôpital se karo to ek step ke baad $\frac{\sin x}{\sin x+x\cos x}$ abhi bhi $0/0$ hai — ek baar aur lagao.
calc-limits-05: Chaaron options alag limits hain — har ek ko khud evaluate karo. $\infty/\infty$ ya $0/0$ form ka matlab value 1 nahi hota.
Rules: $\frac{a^x-1}{x}\to\ln a$ (ye 1 sirf $a=e$ pe hai); $\infty/\infty$ pe L'Hôpital lagao; $x\to\infty$ wale mein $u=\frac1x$ substitute karo.
Pehla option try karo: L'Hôpital se $\frac{\ln x}{x}$ ban jaata hai $\frac{1/x}{1}$ — ye $x\to\infty$ pe kahan jaata hai? Isi tarah baaki teen ek-ek karke check karo.
calc-one-sided-01: $|x-2|$ ka sign is baat pe depend karta hai ki $x$ 2 se bada hai ya chhota — isliye $x\to2^+$ aur $x\to2^-$ alag-alag dekhne padenge.
Rule: limit tabhi exist karti hai jab left limit = right limit. $x>2$ pe $|x-2|=x-2$, aur $x<2$ pe $|x-2|=-(x-2)$.
Right side: $f=\frac{x-2}{x-2}=1$, to $x\to2^+$ pe value 1. Ab left side khud nikalo aur dono compare karo. Trap: sirf ek side dekh ke ruk jaana.
calc-one-sided-02: Floor function $x=3$ pe jump karta hai, isliye 3 se thoda neeche aur thoda upar values alag hain — left limit ke liye $\lfloor 3\rfloor$ seedha mat lagao.
$2\le x<3$ pe $\lfloor x\rfloor$ ek constant hai aur $3\le x<4$ pe doosra constant. Left limit pehle interval se aati hai, right limit doosre se.
Example lo: $x=2.99$ pe $\lfloor x\rfloor=2$ — yahi left limit hai. Ab $x=3.01$ pe nikalo aur dono jodo. Trap: left limit ko $\lfloor3\rfloor=3$ le lena.
calc-one-sided-03: Left piece $\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}$ mein $x=1$ daaloge to $0/0$ — pehle factor karke cancel karo. Aur yaad rakho, $f(1)=2$ limit decide nahi karta.
Limit ke liye left limit ($x<1$ wala piece) aur right limit ($2x+1$) alag nikalo; dono equal hon tabhi limit exist karti hai. $x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)$.
Left: $x\ne1$ pe $\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1}=x+1$, ab $x\to1^-$ lagao. Right: $2x+1$ mein $x\to1^+$ khud karo. Trap: $f(1)=2$ dekh ke limit bhi wahi maan lena.
calc-one-sided-04: $x\to0^-$ hai — sirf left side, yaani $x$ negative. Square root ke andar se bahar nikalte waqt sign ka dhyan rakhna padega.
Identity: $1-\cos2x=2\sin^2x$, to $\sqrt{1-\cos2x}=\sqrt2\,|\sin x|$. Mod zaroori hai kyunki $\sqrt{\sin^2x}=|\sin x|$.
$x<0$ ke paas $\sin x<0$, to $|\sin x|=-\sin x$. Ab $\frac{x}{-\sqrt2\sin x}$ mein $\frac{x}{\sin x}\to1$ use karo. Trap: mod hata ke $+\sin x$ likhne se sign ulta ho jaata hai.
calc-one-sided-05: Sab kuch exponent $\frac1x$ pe depend karta hai — $x$ 0 ke left se aaye ya right se, $\frac1x$ ka sign badal jaata hai.
Pehle likho $x\to0^+$ aur $x\to0^-$ pe $\frac1x$ kis taraf jaata hai. Phir: $e^{t}\to\infty$ jab $t\to+\infty$, aur $e^{t}\to0$ jab $t\to-\infty$. Two-sided limit tabhi exist jab dono sides equal.
Example: $x=-0.01$ lo, to $\frac1x=-100$ — $e^{-100}$ kitna bada ya chhota? Isse left wale do options judge karo, phir $x=+0.01$ se baaki. Trap: dono sides ko same maan lena.
calc-continuity-const-01: Continuity at $x=2$: left piece ($x\le2$) ki value aur right piece ka limit barabar hone chahiye. Isse $k$ ki ek equation milegi.
Right side pehle nikalo: $5(2)-1=9$. Left mein 2 ka square lena mat bhoolo ($4k$, $2k$ nahi) aur $+3$ bhi rakho. Ab $k$ solve karo.
calc-continuity-const-02: $x=3$ pe $\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}$ $0/0$ deta hai — iska matlab value 0 nahi hai, pehle cancel karna padega. $k$ ko us limit ke barabar hona hai.
$x\ne3$ pe $(x-3)$ cancel karo — kya bacha? Usme $x=3$ daalo. Trap: factor $(x+3)$ ka $+3$ chhod ke sirf $x$ bacha lena.
calc-continuity-const-03: Teen pieces aur do unknown $a$, $b$. Continuity at 0 ka matlab left limit $=f(0)=a=$ right limit — do alag equations milengi.
Standard limits: $\frac{\sin kx}{x}\to k$ aur $\frac{e^{kx}-1}{x}\to k$ as $x\to0$. Pehla left piece pe lagao, doosra right piece pe.
Left: $\frac{\sin3x}{x}=3\cdot\frac{\sin3x}{3x}$ — isse $a$ milta hai. Ab right limit ko $a$ ke barabar rakh ke $b$ nikalo, phir jodo. Trap: $\frac{\sin3x}{x}\to1$ maan lena.
calc-continuity-const-04: Do joints hain: $x=1$ aur $x=2$. Har joint pe dono taraf ke pieces milne chahiye — do equations, do unknowns $a$, $b$.
Pehle $x=2$ wali equation solve karo kyunki usme sirf $b$ hai: $4b=8$. Phir woh $b$ $x=1$ wali mein daalo. Trap: $bx^2$ ko $x=2$ pe $2b$ likhna (square bhool jaana).
calc-composition-01: $(f\circ g)(2)$ ka matlab $f(g(2))$ — pehle andar wala $g$, phir bahar wala $f$. Ye product $f(2)\cdot g(2)$ nahi hai.
Inside-out: step 1 $g(2)=2(2)-3$; step 2 us result ko $f(x)=x^2+1$ mein daalo.
$g(2)=1$ aaya — yahin mat ruko, ab isse $f$ mein daalo. Trap: order ulta karke $g(f(2))$ nikal lena.
calc-composition-02: Andar $g(x)=x^2$ hai — $x\ne0$ ke liye $x^2$ hamesha positive hai. To limit ke liye sgn ka sirf ek side matter karta hai.
Continuity check: $\lim_{x\to0}h(x)$ nikalo aur use $h(0)=\operatorname{sgn}(g(0))$ se compare karo. Dono equal hon tabhi continuous.
$x=0.1$ ya $x=-0.1$ lo: dono mein $g=0.01>0$, to $h=\operatorname{sgn}(0.01)=1$. Ab $h(0)$ alag se nikalo aur compare karo. Trap: sgn ka jump dekh ke limit DNE bol dena.
calc-composition-03: $f(f(3))$ mein $f$ do baar lagana hai: pehle $f(3)$, phir us result pe dobara $f$.
$f(3)=\frac{4}{2}=2$ — yahin mat ruko, isi value pe $f$ dobara lagao. Trap: numerator aur denominator ulte likh dena.
calc-composition-04: Har option alag function hai — har ek ka formula pehle simplify karo (kai ek constant ban jaate hain), phir $x=0$ pe jump hai ya nahi dekho.
Inside-out socho: $g$ sirf $\pm1$ output deta hai, aur $f(x)=|x|\ge0$ hamesha. Product $f\cdot g$ ko $x>0$ aur $x<0$ pe alag likho.
Example: $g\circ f$ mein pehle $f(x)=|x|$, jo kabhi negative nahi — to $g$ ka kaunsa branch lagega? Baaki teen bhi aise hi simplify karo. Trap: maan lena ki composition se jump hamesha hat jaata hai.
calc-composition-05: Bahar $\ln$ hai, andar $\frac{e^{2x}-1}{x}$ — inside-out chalo: pehle andar ka limit, phir $\ln$ lagao ($\ln$ continuous hai).
Standard: $\frac{e^{kx}-1}{x}\to k$ as $x\to0$; yahan $k=2$. Phir limit $=\ln(\text{andar ka limit})$.
Andar ka factor 2 mat bhoolo — use 1 maan liya to $\ln1=0$ galat aayega. Inner limit ke baad $\ln$ lagana bhi mat bhoolo, aur 3 decimal tak round karo.
calc-differentiability-01: Har function ke liye $x=0$ pe left derivative aur right derivative compare karo. Corner (dono slopes alag) matlab not differentiable.
$x>0$ pe $|x|=x$ aur $x<0$ pe $|x|=-x$ likh ke har function ko piecewise banao, phir dono pieces ka slope $x=0$ pe nikalo.
Example: $|x|$ right pe $x$, left pe $-x$, to slopes $1$ aur $-1$. Isi tarah $x|x|=\pm x^2$, $|x|^3$ aur ReLU ke dono slopes nikalo. Trap: continuous hai to differentiable maan lena.
calc-differentiability-02: Differentiable at $x=1$ ke liye do conditions: values milein (continuity) aur slopes milein. Do unknowns, do equations.
Slope wali equation pehle solve karo: $2x$ ko $x=1$ pe nikalo, wahi $b$ hai. Phir continuity mein daalo — $+2$ mat chhodna. Trap: sirf continuity dekh ke koi bhi pair chun lena.
calc-differentiability-03: Teeno terms ke corners alag-alag dhundo: $|x^2-4|$ wahan corner banata hai jahan $x^2-4=0$; $|x|$ aur $|x^3|$ ko $x=0$ pe check karo.
Rule: $|h(x)|$ ka corner simple root pe hota hai jahan $h'\ne0$. Lekin $|x^3|=|x|^3$ ka derivative $3x|x|$ hai, jo 0 pe smooth hai.
$x^2-4=0$ ke roots nikalo — dono pe slope $2x\ne0$, to dono corners hain. Ab $x=0$ ko alag se socho. Trap: $|x^3|$ ko bhi corner maan ke 0 ko do baar ginna.
calc-differentiability-04: $r(x)=\max(0,x)$ ka 0 pe corner hai, lekin yahan $g=r^2$ hai — squaring corner ko smooth kar sakta hai. Dono sides ka slope check karo.
Piecewise: $x<0$ pe $g=0$, $x\ge0$ pe $g=x^2$. Phir $g'(0^-)$ aur $g'(0^+)=\lim_{h\to0^+}\frac{h^2}{h}$ compare karo.
Left side pe $g=0$ constant hai, to $g'(0^-)=0$. Ab right side wala limit khud nikalo. Trap: ReLU ka right slope 1 seedha $g$ pe laga dena.
calc-differentiability-05: $x|x|$ mein mod hai, to $x\ge0$ aur $x<0$ pe formula alag hai — dono sides ka derivative alag nikalo, phir ek expression mein jodo.
$x\ge0$: $f=x^2$; $x<0$: $f=-x^2$. Dono ka derivative lo aur $x=0$ pe left/right values check karo.
Right side ($x>0$): $f'=2x$. Left side ka derivative khud nikalo, dono ka sign dekho aur options se match karo. Trap: poore domain pe $f=x^2$ maan lena.
calc-derivative-rules-01: $f'''(0)$ chahiye — teen baar product rule lagana padega. Shortcut bhi hai: $f^{(n)}(0)=n!\times(x^n$ ka Maclaurin coefficient$)$.
Product rule se: $f'=(x^2+2x)e^x$, $f''=(x^2+4x+2)e^x$ — ek baar aur differentiate karke $x=0$ daalo. Trap: $f''(0)$ pe ruk jaana ya cross terms bhool jaana.
calc-derivative-rules-02: $\ln$ ke andar $x^2+1$ hai, sirf $x$ nahi — chain rule lagega. Aur derivative chahiye, function ki value $\ln2$ nahi.
Chain rule: $\frac{d}{dx}\ln u=\frac{1}{u}\cdot u'$, yahan $u=x^2+1$ aur $u'=2x$.
Derivative $\frac{2x}{x^2+1}$ banta hai; ab isme $x=1$ daalo. Trap: chain factor $2x$ chhod ke sirf $\frac{1}{x^2+1}$ likhna.
calc-derivative-rules-03: $\sin(x^2)$ ka second derivative — pehle chain rule, phir $f'$ ek product ban jaata hai to product rule bhi. Point pe $x^2=\pi/2$ hai, jo sab simplify karega.
Simplify: $f''=2\cos(x^2)-4x^2\sin(x^2)$. Ab $x^2=\frac{\pi}{2}$ daalo — $\cos\frac{\pi}{2}$ aur $\sin\frac{\pi}{2}$ kya hain? Trap: minus sign ya inner factor 2 chhod dena.
calc-derivative-rules-04: $\frac{1}{1-x}$ ko baar baar differentiate karo to ek pattern banta hai. Ya Maclaurin series $1+x+x^2+\dots$ ka $x^5$ coefficient use karo.

Ek step aur: $f'''=6(1-x)^{-4}$ — har baar chain rule ka $-1$ aur power ka minus cancel hote hain, sign positive rehta hai. Pattern 5th derivative tak badhao. Trap: sirf coefficient likhna, $n!$ se multiply na karna.
calc-derivative-rules-05: Har option ko actual derivative se compare karna hai. Ek option khud ek derivative hai — use bhi nikal ke dekho.
Quotient rule: $\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)'=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$ with $u=x$, $v=1+x$, $u'=v'=1$. Ya $\frac{x}{1+x}=1-\frac{1}{1+x}$ likh lo.
Numerator: $u'v-uv'=1\cdot(1+x)-x\cdot1$ — ise simplify karo. Phir $\frac{d}{dx}\left(-\frac{1}{1+x}\right)$ alag se nikalo. Trap: numerator mein minus ki jagah plus lagana.
calc-taylor-01: $e^{2x}$ ki series chahiye — $e^u$ ki series mein $u=2x$ rakho. $x^3$ term mein $(2x)^3$ aayega, sirf $x^3$ nahi.
$2^3$ aur $3!$ alag-alag nikalo, phir divide karke 2 decimal tak round karo. Trap: $3!$ ki jagah sirf 3 se divide karna, ya $2^3$ bhool jaana.
calc-taylor-02: Expansion point $x=1$ hai, 0 nahi — isliye terms $(x-1)$ ki powers mein honge. $\ln(1+x)$ ki 0 wali series seedha mat chipkao.
Pehle $f(1)=\ln1$ nikalo — ye 1 nahi hai. Phir $f'(1)$ aur $f''(1)$ ki values sign ke saath lagao. Trap: $f''$ ka minus sign chhod dena.
calc-taylor-03: Do series ka product hai — $x^4$ sirf ek term se nahi aata. Har woh pair jiski powers ka sum 4 ho, sab collect karne hain.
$e^x$ ke coefficients: $1,1,\frac12,\frac16,\frac1{24}$; $\cos x$ ke: $1,0,-\frac12,0,\frac1{24}$. $x^4$ ka coefficient $=\sum_k a_k\,b_{4-k}$.
$\cos x$ ke odd coefficients 0 hain, to sirf $k=0,2,4$ bachte hain. Pehla: $a_0b_4=1\cdot\frac1{24}$. Baaki do khud likho aur jodo. Trap: cross term $\frac12\cdot\left(-\frac12\right)$ bhool jaana.
calc-taylor-04: $\sqrt{4.2}$ ko $x=4$ ke paas expand karo kyunki $\sqrt4=2$ exact hai. Yahan $h=4.2-4=0.2$, aur second-order term bhi chahiye.
$f(4)=2$, $f'(4)=\frac14$, $f''(4)=-\frac14\cdot\frac18$. Ab $h=0.2$ daal ke teeno terms jodo, 4 decimal tak. Trap: $\frac{1}{2!}$ bhool jaana ya $f''$ ka minus chhod dena.
calc-taylor-05: Har statement alag cheez pooch raha hai: ek derivative, do coefficients, ek convergence. Coefficient aur derivative same cheez nahi hote.
$\ln(1+x)$ ka general coefficient $\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$ hai (sign alternate karta hai). Aur $f^{(n)}(0)=n!\times(x^n$ ka coefficient$)$.

$f'''(0)$ ke liye pehle $x^3$ ka coefficient formula se nikalo, phir $3!$ se multiply karo. $x=1$ pe series $1-\frac12+\frac13-\dots$ banti hai — alternating series test socho. Trap: $x^2$ coefficient ka sign bhoolna.
calc-series-sums-01: Ye geometric series hai, ratio $r=\frac23$, aur index $n=0$ se shuru hai — pehla term $\left(\frac23\right)^0=1$ hai.
Denominator pehle nikalo: $1-\frac23=\frac13$. Ab 1 ko isse divide karo. Trap: $n=1$ wala formula $\frac{r}{1-r}$ laga dena.
calc-series-sums-02: $\frac{1}{n(n+2)}$ ko partial fractions mein todo — terms telescope honge, lekin cancellation do step door hoga ($n$ aur $n+2$), consecutive nahi.

Kuch terms likho: $\frac12\left[(1-\frac13)+(\frac12-\frac14)+(\frac13-\frac15)+\dots\right]$. Kaunse positive terms kabhi cancel nahi hote? Unhe jodo aur $\frac12$ se multiply karo. Trap: sirf pehla term bachana.
calc-series-sums-03: Har term mein $n$ ka factor hai, to ye plain geometric nahi hai. Consecutive terms ka ratio $\to\frac12<1$, to series converge karti hai — ab sum chahiye.
$\sum x^n=\frac{1}{1-x}$ ko differentiate karo: $\sum nx^{n-1}=\frac{1}{(1-x)^2}$. Yahan $x^n$ chahiye, to $x$ se multiply karo: $\sum nx^n=\frac{x}{(1-x)^2}$.
Ab $x=\frac12$ daalo: denominator $\left(1-\frac12\right)^2=\frac14$. Numerator khud lagao. Trap: $x$ se multiply karna bhool jaana.
calc-series-sums-04: Fraction ko do parts mein todo: $\frac{3^n}{6^n}$ aur $\frac{2^n}{6^n}$ — dono alag geometric series hain. Index $n=1$ se shuru hai.
Pehli series: $\frac{1/2}{1-1/2}=1$. Ab $r=\frac13$ wali khud nikalo aur jodo. Trap: ratios jod ke ek hi series $r=\frac56$ bana dena, ya $n=0$ se sum lena.
calc-series-sums-05: Har series pe alag test lagega: terms 0 ki taraf jaate hain ya nahi, geometric hai ya nahi, alternating hai ya nahi.
Tests: terms $\not\to0$ to diverge; geometric $|r|<1$ pe converge; alternating series jiske terms decreasing to 0 hon, converge; $\sum\frac{1}{n^p}$ sirf $p>1$ pe converge.
Pehla option: $\frac{n}{n+1}$ jab $n\to\infty$ kahan jaata hai? Usse n-th term test lagao. Baaki teen ko upar ke tests se ek-ek karke judge karo. Trap: terms $\to0$ dekh ke converge maan lena.
calc-extrema-01: Local minimum ki **value** chahiye, location $x$ nahi. Pehle critical points nikalo, phir decide karo kaunsa min hai.
$f'(x)=3x^2-6x=0$ solve karo; classify ke liye $f''(x)=6x-6$ ka sign dekho ($>0$ matlab min).
$3x(x-2)=0$ se $x=0,2$. $f''(0)=-6<0$, to $x=0$ max hai. Ab min point pe $f$ ki value nikalo. Trap: $x$ ki value ko hi report kar dena.
calc-extrema-02: Closed interval $[0,3]$ pe absolute max chahiye — stationary points ke saath dono endpoints bhi check karo. Jo stationary point interval ke bahar ho, use chhod do.
$f'=3x^2-3=0\Rightarrow x=\pm1$; sirf $x=1$ interval mein hai. Candidates: $x=0,1,3$.
$f(0)=0$, $f(1)=1-3=-2$. Ab $f(3)$ nikalo aur teeno compare karo. Trap: right endpoint bhool jaana, ya $x=-1$ use karna jo $[0,3]$ mein hai hi nahi.
calc-extrema-03: $x^4$ mein $f'(0)$ aur $f''(0)$ dono 0 aate hain — socho ye second-derivative test ke baare mein kya batata hai, aur phir kaunsa test lagana chahiye.
Jab $f''=0$ ho to first-derivative test lagao: $f'=4x^3$ ka sign $x=0$ ke left aur right dekho. Inflection ke liye $f''$ ka sign change hona zaroori hai.
$x=-0.1$ aur $x=0.1$ pe $f'=4x^3$ ka sign nikalo. $-\to+$ ya $+\to-$, kaunsa pattern kya batata hai? Trap: $f''=0$ dekh ke seedha inflection maan lena.
calc-extrema-04: Domain $[0,\infty)$ hai, to endpoint $x=0$ bhi candidate hai. Statements derivative sign, inflection aur global max/min ke baare mein hain — pehle $f'$ aur $f''$ nikalo.
Product rule: $f'=(1-x)e^{-x}$, $f''=(x-2)e^{-x}$. $e^{-x}>0$ hamesha, to sign sirf bracket se decide hota hai.
$f''(1)$ ke liye $(1-2)e^{-1}$ ka sign dekho. Baaki: $f'=0$ kahan hai, $f''$ sign kahan badalta hai, aur $f(0)$ vs $x>0$ pe $f$. Trap: endpoint $x=0$ ignore karna.
calc-extrema-05: Closed interval $[0,3]$ — absolute max/min ke candidates hain stationary points aur dono endpoints. Sabki values compare karni hain.
$f(1)=2-9+12=5$, $f(2)=16-36+24=4$. Ab dono endpoints $f(0)$, $f(3)$ nikalo aur charon compare karo. Trap: sirf stationary points compare karna.
calc-convexity-01: Har function ko poore $\mathbb{R}$ pe check karo — sirf ek interval pe convex hona kaafi nahi. Ek option 0 pe differentiable nahi hai, uske liye $f''$ se kaam nahi chalega.
Rule: $f''(x)\ge0$ har $x$ pe ⇒ convex. Jahan $f''$ exist na kare (corner), wahan chord test lagao: kisi bhi do points ke beech ki line graph ke upar ya us par ho.
$x^3$ ke liye $f''=6x$ — $x=-1$ pe iska sign kya hai? Isi tarah $e^x$ aur $-x^2+2x$ ka $f''$ nikalo, aur $|x|$ ko do lines ka max socho. Trap: non-differentiable dekh ke convex na maanna.
calc-convexity-02: Convexity $f''$ se decide hoti hai, $f'$ se nahi. Is quartic mein $-6x^2$ term 0 ke paas convexity tod sakta hai.
$12x^2-12\ge0$ ko 12 se divide karo, phir $x=0$ aur $x=2$ jaise points pe test karke dekho kis region mein $f''\ge0$ hai. Trap: inequality ulti padhna, ya $f'=0$ solve kar dena.
calc-convexity-03: Convex on all of $\mathbb{R}$ ka matlab $f''(x)\ge0$ har $x$ ke liye. $f''$ ek quadratic banega — use kabhi negative nahi hona chahiye.
$f''=12x^2+6ax+12$. Upward quadratic har jagah $\ge0$ tab hai jab discriminant $\le0$: $(6a)^2-4\cdot12\cdot12\le0$.
$36a^2\le576$ simplify karo, $a^2$ ki bound milegi — lekin $c$ bound $|a|$ pe hai, $a^2$ pe nahi. Trap: discriminant mein 4 bhool jaana, ya $ax^3$ ko sirf ek baar differentiate karna.
calc-convexity-04: Har statement 'always true' hona chahiye — ek bhi convex differentiable function counterexample de de to statement galat. $e^x$ aur $x^2$ jaise examples pe test karo.
Teen tools socho: differentiable $f$ ke liye convexity $f'$ ke baare mein kya kehti hai; tangent line graph ke upar hai ya neeche; aur chord graph ke upar rehti hai to local vs global min.
'Minimiser exists' wala statement $e^x$ pe test karo: ye convex hai ($f''=e^x>0$) — kya iska koi minimum point hai? Baaki teen ko $x^2$ jaise example aur upar ke rules se judge karo.
calc-opt-word-01: Do variables aur ek constraint $x+2y=20$ — constraint se ek variable hata ke $xy$ ko ek variable ka function banao. Dhyan: constraint mein $2y$ hai, $y$ nahi.
$P'(y)=20-4y=0$ solve karo, phir $x$ nikalo aur $xy$ calculate karo. Trap: constraint ko $x+y=20$ padh lena.
calc-opt-word-02: Har corner se square kaata, to har side se do baar $x$ ghatega. Volume chahiye, cut $x$ nahi — aur $x$ ka valid range bhi socho.
Product rule: $V'=(12-2x)^2-4x(12-2x)=(12-2x)(12-6x)$. Root $x=6$ volume 0 deta hai — doosra root lo aur $V$ nikalo. Trap: $x$ ko hi report kar dena.
calc-opt-word-03: River ke saath fence nahi chahiye — to sirf teen sides fence hongi: river ke perpendicular do sides ($x$, $x$) aur ek parallel side ($y$).
$A=400x-2x^2$; $A'=400-4x=0$ solve karo, phir $y$ nikalo aur $A=xy$. Trap: teeno sides barabar maan lena, ya chaaron sides fence kar dena.
calc-opt-word-04: Squared distances ka sum minimise karna hai — ye ek variable ka smooth function hai, derivative zero karo. Median ya midpoint wala shortcut yahan nahi chalta.
Bracket simplify karo: $3x-(1+5+6)=0$. Ab $x$ nikalo — 3 se divide karna mat bhoolo. Trap: $x=\sum a_i$ likh dena.
calc-gradient-descent-01: Sirf ek step chahiye, minimiser nahi. Gradient descent mein gradient ke **against** chalte hain.
Pehle $f'(0)=2(0)-4=-4$. Ab $x_1=0-0.1\times(-4)$ — minus-minus ka sign dhyan se. Trap: $+\eta f'$ karke ulti direction mein jaana.
calc-gradient-descent-02: Do steps chahiye ($x_2$). Har step pe gradient naye point pe dobara nikalna hai — pehla step double mat karo.
Step 1: $f'(0)=-6$, to $x_1=0-0.25(-6)=1.5$. Ab $f'(1.5)$ nikalo aur second step lo. Trap: ek hi step pe ruk jaana.
calc-gradient-descent-03: $f=x^2$ convex hai, par step $\eta=1.2$ bada hai. Convergence step size pe depend karti hai — update ko $x_k$ ke multiple ki tarah likho.
$\eta=1.2$ daalo: factor $=1-2(1.2)$. Ise nikalo, phir socho iska absolute value 1 se bada hai ya chhota, aur sign kya hai. Trap: convex hai to converge karega maan lena.
calc-gradient-descent-04: Do variables hain, to gradient ek vector hai — har coordinate ka apna partial derivative. Dono coordinates ke liye same partial mat use karo.
$\nabla f(1,1)=(2,6)$. Ise $0.1$ se multiply karo aur $(1,1)$ mein se **subtract** karo. Trap: add kar dena (ascent) ya $\eta$ bhool jaana.
calc-gradient-descent-05: Loss $w$ ka function hai; $x=2$ aur $y=4$ fixed numbers hain. $\frac{dL}{dw}$ mein chain rule lagega — square ka 2 aur andar ka $x$, dono aayenge.
$w_0=0$ pe $wx-y=0-4=-4$. Ab $2\cdot(-4)\cdot2$ nikalo, phir update lagao. Trap: factor 2 ya chain factor $x$ chhod dena.
